chunks: And Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

"Keep your tongues back (remain silent) and stay in your houses, for no matter will afflict you specifically that does not also afflict the general public, and the Zaydites will remain a shield/protector for you forever."

key_terms.الزَّيْدِيَّةُ: The Zaydites (followers of Zayd ibn Ali)
key_terms.الْزَمُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ: Stay in your houses / Adhere to your homes
key_terms.الْعَامَّةَ: The general public / The common people
key_terms.كُفُّوا أَلْسِنَتَكُمْ: Keep your tongues back / Remain silent

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq advise staying in houses and remaining silent?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises his followers to maintain silence and remain in their homes as a strategy of political quietism. This ensures that any tribulation or punishment from the ruling authorities will be shared by the general population rather than targeting the Shias specifically, as the Zaydites (followers of Zayd ibn Ali) serve as a protective buffer or shield between the Shias and the government.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (8) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik al-Fazari from Muhammad bin Ahmad from Ali bin Asbat from some of his companions that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“Keep silent and remain in your houses because no bad will afflict you especially, which will afflict the rest of people, and as long as the (revolutionary) Zaydites will be as a frontstead between you and the governments.”
